Generate a Parameter Frame

Source: R/parClass.R
parframe.Rd

A parameter frame is a data frame with one parameter set per row. The columns fall into three groups: meta-information (e.g. index, value, converged), attributes of an objective function (e.g. data and prior contribution) and the parameters.

Usage

is.parframe(x)

# S3 method for class 'parframe'
x[i, j, drop = FALSE]

# S3 method for class 'parframe'
subset(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'parframe'
rbind(..., deparse.level = 1)

parframe(
  x = NULL,
  parameters = setdiff(colnames(x), c(metanames, objAttributes)),
  metanames = NULL,
  objAttributes = NULL
)

Arguments

x

data frame. Default NULL gives an empty parameter frame.

i

row index in any format; missing keeps all rows. Used alone, as in x[j], it selects columns, as for a data frame.

j

column index in any format; missing keeps all columns.

drop

logical. Default FALSE. TRUE returns a plain data frame or vector instead of a parframe.

...

for subset(), logical expressions in the columns of x; a row is kept where all of them are TRUE. For rbind(), parameter frames with the same columns.

deparse.level

not used.

parameters

character, the names of the parameter columns. Default all columns that are neither in metanames nor in objAttributes.

metanames

character, the names of the meta-information columns. Default NULL.

objAttributes

character, the names of the objective function attributes. Default NULL.

Value

Object of class parframe, a data frame with the attributes parameters, metanames and obj.attributes. is.parframe() returns a logical.

Details

rbind() keeps the attributes of the first frame. Profiles of one parameter computed in parts, such as the left and right side, are joined into one: the repeated optimum is dropped and the points are sorted by constraint.

Parameter frames can be subsetted either by [ , ] or by subset. If [ , index] is used, the names of the removed columns will also be removed from the corresponding attributes, i.e. metanames, obj.attributes and parameters.

See also

as.parframe(), profile(), mstrust()

Examples

pf <- parframe(data.frame(value = c(3, 1, 2), a = c(1, 2, 3), b = c(0, 1, 0)),
               parameters = c("a", "b"), metanames = "value")
pf[pf$value < 3, ]
#>   value a b
#> 1     1 2 1
#> 2     2 3 0
as.parvec(pf)
#> Parameter vector:
#>   a :       2
#>   b :       1
#> 
#> Attributes:
#>   deriv  : <none>
#>   deriv2 : <none>
#>   fixed  : <none>
